# Terms of Service

Version 2026-11-19 · **A first draft, not yet reviewed by a lawyer.**

The agreement for using Welcome Wave.

**For:** Everyone who signs in, and the organisation they work for\
**Accepted by:** Each person, for themselves, in the product.

## In brief

- Welcome Wave turns your organisation's recorded KT sessions, documents and code into cited answers, onboarding plans and review drafts. Agents propose; people decide.
- What your organisation puts in stays its own. We use it only to run the service, and we do not train AI models on it.
- Answers and drafts are written by AI and can be wrong. Check the sources before you rely on one.
- A recording may be added only when everyone in the session was told and agreed.
- Your organisation can leave at any time. An admin can export its records and delete everything.
- What each side owes the other if something goes wrong is limited. Section 14 says how.

## 1. Who this agreement is between

Welcome Wave is run by the company that operates this service. In these terms that is “we” and “us”.

“Your organisation” is the company or team whose workspace you use. It is our customer. “You” are the person signed in.

If you create an organisation, you accept these terms for it and confirm that you are allowed to. If you were invited, your organisation has already accepted them, and you accept the parts that speak to a person: your account (3), acceptable use (4), AI features (6) and recordings (7).

| Who we are | Details |
|---|---|
| Company | The company that operates this service |
| Postal address | The operator's registered office |
| Contact | The support contact for this service |
| Privacy requests | The privacy contact for this service |

These documents are part of the agreement: [Acceptable Use](ACCEPTABLE_USE.md), [Privacy Policy](PRIVACY.md), [Recording and AI Notice](RECORDING.md), [Data Processing Agreement](DPA.md) and [Sub-processors](SUBPROCESSORS.md). If your organisation has signed a separate written agreement or order with us, that document wins where the two differ.

## 2. The service

Welcome Wave reads the repositories your organisation connects and stores the documents and KT recordings its people add. It uses AI to write notes, answer questions with sources, and draft onboarding plans and pull request reviews.

We may change how the service works. If a change takes away something your organisation relies on, we tell its admins beforehand, and it may end the agreement under section 12.

We work to keep the service available and safe. We do not promise a level of uptime unless a written order says so.

A feature marked as a pilot or beta is offered as it is, and may change or stop.

## 3. Your account

You sign in with Google, or with an email address and a password. Sign-in is handled by Google's Identity Platform. Your password goes to Google, never to us.

Keep your sign-in to yourself. If you think someone else has used it, tell your admin and write to the support contact for this service.

Your organisation's admins decide who is a member and what role each person has, and can deactivate an account. Your organisation is responsible for what its members do in the service.

The service is for people at work. You must be 18 or older.

## 4. Acceptable use

Use Welcome Wave for your organisation's own onboarding and knowledge transfer, within [Acceptable Use](ACCEPTABLE_USE.md). In short: add only what you have the right to add, do not record people who have not been told, and do not attack the service or try to reach another organisation's data.

## 5. Your organisation's content

Code, documents, recordings, questions and everything else your organisation's people put in remain your organisation's. We claim no ownership of any of it.

Your organisation lets us store this content, process it, show it to its members and pass it to the providers in [Sub-processors](SUBPROCESSORS.md), only to run, secure and support the service for it.

We do not sell it. We do not use it to train or fine-tune AI models.

Your organisation confirms that it has the right to connect each repository and to add each document and recording, and that doing so breaks no law and no promise made to someone else.

We may use operational figures that hold none of this content, such as request counts, timings and error rates, to run and improve the service. If you send us ideas about the product, we may use them freely.

## 6. AI features

Answers, notes, plans and reviews are written by Google's Gemini models from your organisation's content. They can be wrong, incomplete or out of date.

Every answer shows the sources it was built from. When the assistant cannot support an answer with sources, it says it does not have enough information, and the question can go to a person.

Agents propose; people decide. A plan, a review or a change to a document takes effect only when a person with the right role approves it. No agent can change a role, grant access or write to your repositories.

You and your organisation remain responsible for decisions made with the help of these outputs. Do not make an output the only basis for a decision that seriously affects a person, such as their pay or their employment.

## 7. Recordings

Welcome Wave does not record calls. Your organisation records a session with its own meeting tool. A member then adds the file, or Welcome Wave imports it from the organisation's Google Drive when the session was booked through its Google Calendar.

Before a recording is added, a member confirms that every participant was told about the recording and agreed. Welcome Wave keeps who confirmed and when, and refuses the recording without it.

Recording law differs from place to place, and some places require every participant's agreement. Meeting that law is your organisation's responsibility. [Recording and AI Notice](RECORDING.md) explains what happens to a recording and what a host must do.

## 8. Access to your code

Welcome Wave reads repositories. It has no way to write to them: it cannot push, comment, approve or merge.

Depending on how the service is set up, it reads through a GitHub App with read-only permissions, or by repository address with a token the operator provides, which should be read-only. Your organisation can withdraw this access at GitHub at any time.

## 9. Services your organisation connects

Your organisation may connect GitHub, Google Calendar, Meet and Drive, and Calendly. Its own agreements with those providers cover what they do, and we are not responsible for their services.

## 10. Fees

The price, if there is one, is what your organisation and we agreed in writing: an order, a pilot agreement or an invoice. The product itself takes no payment.

Unless that agreement says otherwise, invoices are due within 30 days, and amounts exclude taxes such as GST, which we add where the law requires. Fees already paid are not refunded when your organisation ends the agreement early, except where section 12 or the law says otherwise.

## 11. Confidentiality

Each of us keeps the other's confidential information private, uses it only for this agreement, and protects it with at least reasonable care. Your organisation's content is its confidential information.

This does not cover information that is public, was already known, was developed independently, or was lawfully received from someone else. If the law requires one of us to disclose something, that side tells the other first where the law allows.

## 12. Term, suspension and ending

The agreement starts when your organisation is created and runs until one of us ends it.

Your organisation may end it at any time: an admin deletes the organisation in Settings, or writes to us. We may end it with 30 days' written notice. If we end it without cause, we refund fees paid for the time after it ends.

Either of us may end it at once if the other seriously breaks it and does not put that right within 30 days of being told.

We may suspend access where we must: to stop a security threat, to stop use that breaks the law or [Acceptable Use](ACCEPTABLE_USE.md), or when an invoice is more than 30 days late after a reminder. We tell the admins as soon as we can, and restore access when the cause is gone.

Until the end, an admin can export the organisation's records and delete everything. If anything remains, we delete it within 30 days after the end, unless the law requires us to keep it. Copies in backups go when the backups expire.

Confidentiality, fees owed, liability and the general terms outlast the agreement.

## 13. What we promise, and what we do not

We provide the service with reasonable skill and care, and we keep to [Privacy Policy](PRIVACY.md) and [Data Processing Agreement](DPA.md).

Beyond that, and as far as the law allows, the service comes as it is. We do not promise that it will run without interruption or error, or that an AI output is correct or fit for a particular purpose.

## 14. Liability

Nothing in these terms limits liability that the law does not allow to be limited, such as liability for fraud, or for death or personal injury caused by negligence.

Otherwise, neither of us is liable to the other for lost profits, lost revenue or lost business, or for indirect or consequential loss.

Otherwise, the total either of us may owe the other under this agreement is limited to the fees your organisation paid or owed us for the 12 months before the event that led to the claim.

These limits do not reduce the fees your organisation owes.

## 15. Claims by others

Your organisation will defend us against a claim by someone else that arises from its content, from a recording made or added without the notice or agreement the law requires, or from use that breaks [Acceptable Use](ACCEPTABLE_USE.md). It will pay what a court awards, or what a settlement it approves costs.

We will defend your organisation in the same way against a claim that the service itself infringes someone's intellectual property rights. This does not cover your organisation's content or outputs made from it.

The side asking to be defended must tell the other promptly, let it run the defence, and give reasonable help.

## 16. Changes to these terms

We may update these terms. Each version carries its date. When a new version is published, you are asked to accept it in the product, and your acceptance is recorded with that version.

If a change reduces your organisation's rights, we tell its admins at least 30 days before it takes effect, and your organisation may end the agreement before then.

## 17. General

- **Law.** These terms are governed by the laws of the place where the operator is established.
- **Courts.** Disputes go to the courts of that place. Rights that the law of your own country gives you, and that cannot be signed away, stay in place.
- **Notices.** Notices to us go to the support contact for this service, or by post to the operator's registered office. Notices to your organisation go to its admins, at the email addresses on their accounts.
- **Transfer.** Neither of us may transfer this agreement without the other's written consent, except to a successor in a merger or a sale of the business, who must honour it.
- **Events outside our control.** Neither of us is liable for a failure caused by something beyond its reasonable control, such as an outage at a cloud or network provider, for as long as it lasts.
- **Whole agreement.** These terms, the documents named in section 1 and any written order are the whole agreement. If part of it cannot be enforced, the rest stands. Not enforcing a right once does not give it up.
